column5: Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life (John 14:6), the full expression of God’s truth, wisdom, and revelation. This embodied expression, that is, the Word (logos), existed from the beginning and became flesh to dwell among us (John 1:1, 14). Jesus’ systematic teachings are His doctrine (***didaskalia***), and in following His commandments (to obey, to keep, to guard) (***entolē)*** we become His disciples (***mathētēs***).

column4: Imagine a master architect, the greatest builder in all history, whose vision, knowledge, and wisdom surpass all others. He alone understands the perfect design for an enduring, unshakable structure. His understanding is not derived from others-it is inherent within Him. He is the source of all architectural wisdom, and every sound building finds its origin in His design. This architect represents Jesus, the Logos-the full and complete embodiment of God’s truth, wisdom, and revelation (John 1:1, John 14:6).
column5: Imagine a master architect, the greatest builder in history, whose vision, knowledge, and wisdom surpass all others. He alone understands the perfect design of a durable, unshakable structure. His understanding is not derived from others—it is intrinsic to Him. He is the source of all architectural wisdom, and the foundation of every strong building is found in His design. This architect represents Jesus, the Logos—the complete and perfect embodiment of God’s truth, wisdom, and revelation (John 1:1, John 14:6).

column4: To bring His design to life, the architect creates a **detailed blueprint**-a structured plan that contains the principles, proportions, and foundational truths necessary for constructing a building that will stand firm. Without this blueprint, no one could build correctly. This blueprint represents Jesus’ structured teaching, His doctrine (***didaskalia***) — the framework through which divine truth is understood and applied (Titus 2:1, 1 Timothy 4:13). His doctrine is not merely theoretical knowledge; it is the means by which His wisdom is communicated and preserved so that all who follow Him can build their lives on the right foundation.
column5: To put His design into practice, the architect creates a **detailed blueprint**—an organized plan consisting of the principles, proportions, and foundational truths necessary to build a structure that will stand firm. Without this blueprint no one can build correctly. This blueprint represents Jesus’ systematic teaching, His doctrine (***didaskalia***) — the framework through which divine truth is understood and applied (Titus 2:1, 1 Timothy 4:13). His doctrine is not merely theoretical knowledge; it is the very means by which His wisdom is transmitted and preserved so that all who follow Him can build their lives on the right foundation.

column4: However, a blueprint alone is not enough. The architect also provides **precise instructions**, detailing how each part of the structure should be assembled, where each beam must be placed, and how every element should align with His perfect design. These specific instructions represent His commands **(Entolē**)-the actionable directives that govern obedience (John 14:15, Matthew 28:20). His commands are not arbitrary rules; they are the necessary steps to ensure the building stands strong, aligned with the original blueprint. To ignore or alter His commands would be to compromise the integrity of the entire structure.
column5: However, the blueprint alone is not enough. The architect also provides **precise instructions**, which state how to join each part of the structure, where to place each beam, and how to harmonize every element according to His perfect design. These specific instructions represent His commandments **(Entolē**)-the practical directives that regulate obedience (John 14:15, Matthew 28:20). His commandments are not arbitrary rules; they are the necessary steps that ensure the building stands firm and conforms to the original blueprint. To ignore or alter His commandments is to jeopardize the integrity of the entire structure.

column4: Now, imagine that the architect gathers a group of **apprentices**-those who desire to learn from Him, build under His guidance, and one day teach others how to construct buildings that endure. These apprentices study His blueprint carefully, listen to His instructions attentively, and apply His commands faithfully in their work. They do not build according to their own ideas but according to the master’s design. These apprentices represent the disciples **(Mathētēs**)-those who observe, obey, and internalize Jesus’ teachings, aligning their lives with His Word (Matthew 28:19-20, John 8:31). The more they study under the architect, the more skilled they become, eventually teaching and training others in His ways.
column5: Now imagine that the architect gathers a group of **disciples**—those who want to learn from Him, build under His supervision, and one day teach others to build structures that endure. These disciples study His blueprint carefully, listen attentively to His instructions, and faithfully carry out His commandments in their work. They build not by their own opinions but according to the Master’s design. These disciples **(Mathētēs**)-are those who observe, obey, and internalize Jesus’ teachings, shaping their lives according to His Word (Matthew 28:19-20, John 8:31). The longer they remain under the Master’s training, the more skilled they become, until they too teach and train others in His ways.

column4: 1.  **Opening Question (Icebreaker)** - *“What is one teaching or belief that had a major impact on your faith journey?”*
column5: 1.  **Opening Question (Icebreaker)** - *“What is one teaching or belief that has had a major impact on your journey of faith؟”*

column4: 2.  **Digging Deeper** - *“How does doctrine shape not only what we believe, but how we live?”*
column5: 2.  **Going Deeper** - *“Teaching not only shapes what we believe، but also how we live؟”*

column4: 3.  **Practical Application** - *“What steps can we take to ensure we’re growing in sound doctrine while guarding against false teaching?*
column5: 3.  **Practical Application** - *“What steps can we take so that we continue to grow in sound teaching and also keep guarding against false teaching؟*
